text: [Music] This is Ba Na Hills. Lush forested mountains. Mist shrouded gardens. [Music] And an adventure wonderland [Music]. Atop the Chua Mountain, 25 kilometres west of the city of Da Nang, resides Sun world's Ba Na Hills. It was originally established in 1919 by French colonists as a retreat for French tourists, but has since grown into a major tourist destination and boasts many unique attractions. After a 40-minute car journey from Da Nang, you arrive at the foothills of the mountain where you embark on the world's longest cable car journey, delivering you safely to the top, 1.5 kilometres above sea level. The best way to get there is to book a Grab via the app. Be sure to wear your seatbelt though, the roads are dangerous in Vietnam. Once we arrived our driver showed us to the ticket office. Tickets cost 850 000 Dong that day, but ticket prices vary throughout the year. You also get the option to buy a buffet lunch for an extra 350 000, but we chose not to. So here we are. The first escalator takes you up to a chinese-style garden. It's peaceful here. A stark contrast to the city below. [Music] Moving onwards, the escalators seem to go on forever... and ever... …and ever. But we eventually reached a ticket officers. All the staff were very friendly, and spoke good English. Ahhh, finally we made it. [Music] The cable car launched us out, high above, with stunning vistas of the mountain below. [Music] The mountains rose in the distance like enormous green waves. [Music] Dense, luscious jungle below. As we rose higher the mist became thicker and thicker, until the approaching cable cars appeared and disappeared like ghosts. Finally we make it to the top, greeted by a scene of eclectic buildings and signs of further expansion. [Music] So here we are, at Toulouse station. Let's head towards the barrel to see what we can find. This area had a Germanic feel, with beer and bratwurst available. Imposing golden statues ahead of us. [Music] Onwards and upwards towards the central area. Along the way, there were rose gardens, performers, plenty of restaurants and breath taking views. This is the central area, [Music] and the little hut there is the information centre. Be sure to pick up a map. This is the original church built by the French. The French influence can be seen everywhere in this area. [Music] We grabbed some Vietnamese coffee (just do it). DO IT! JUST DO IT! [Music] Phewww. I think I did it... What'd you reckon Bill? [Music] Moving upwards through the lanes you pass many restaurants and hotels and we were surprised by more entertainers. [Music] A quick pit stop for food. They have all sorts here, even for the fussiest eaters. Next, we headed for the Alpine Coaster. Along the way another surprise performance [Music]. (I love you! I love you too!) The Alpine Coaster. It's more of a toboggan really, with the rear rider controlling the brakes. You can choose to brake if you'd like, or don't break at all. So long as you don't hit the rider in front. You also have the option to purchase two different photos from your ride they're eighty thousand Dong each. [Music] The end of the ride spits you into a funfair area. There are lots of carnival games and rides here, as well as a museum upstairs [Music]. We didn't hang around too long though, as time was pressing and we wanted to move on to the next area [Music]. The Golden Bridge or Cau Vang in Vietnamese. It's an iconic bridge featuring two enormous hands, cradling a 150 meter gold strip high above the clouds. To get there you need to take a cable car from the Louvre station to Bordeaux. [Music] We went around 2PM and the bridge was quite crowded. With more clustering around the giant hands. Everyone wanted to snap the perfect shot. While I let the clips roll, I'll give some general guidance. [Music] Get to the resort early, it's a lot larger than you think and you need at least one full day to explore it properly. I'd also bring cash as not all vendors accept card. Additionally, they seem to charge more for transactions made with card. There are ATMs available at Ba Na Station at the foothills of the mountain, before you get on the cable car. Also if you were wondering, you can still receive data at the top of the mountain [Music]. We actually returned to the bridge at a later time and it was much quieter. The Mist had rolled in thick and heavy now and added to the drama of the scene. It really felt like you're up in the clouds, cradled in the hands of an ancient stone giant. [Music] Sadly though, we couldn't get a clear view of the landscape below, but maybe you'll have more luck if you visit. If you did want a photo when no one's around then I recommend booking a night at one of the hotels here, though expect to get up early. [Music] At the end of the bridge there are more giant stone statues. A common theme in this area. Let's move down towards the gardens. Along the way you might sneak a glimpse of the Lunar Castle through the mist [Music]. There's a quiet balcony here overlooking the gardens and a great place for a snack [Music]. Heading further down we found a wine cellar, and nearby... a bar! There were a surprising amount of options, and this was an exceptionally peaceful part of the resort to relax. [Music] Moving inside the bar, you can see the array of available wines. And through the back door a little surprise [Music]. There were dimly lit corridors... Random miniature scenes... The sound of water flowing in the distance... [Music] ...this was of course The Wine Cellar. And right through this door is the exit, right where we saw the sign at the start. Further down from the wine bar are more gardens, and what would be stunning views on a clear day. [Music] There's also a maze here. We decided to check it out - but be warned something terrifying lies within this maze. [Music] In a word, this part of the resort is tranquil. A place to be by yourself but also connect with the world around you. The day was getting long and the cable cars end their service at 5 PM. Not wanting to walk down the mountain we headed back to the central area to conclude our trip. All right everyone thank you so much for watching. Be sure to check out the next episode, and as always like and subscribe! [Music]
